title: Choose controls for the attacker you actually have
description: Select a threat, defense stack, and release count. The lab separates update confidentiality, statistical privacy, poisoning resistance, and dropout resilience instead of treating federated learning as one privacy switch.

threats.label: Curious coordinator
threats.detail: The server follows the protocol but tries to inspect an individual client's update.
threats.observableSignal: Audit access to round artifacts, secure-aggregation transcript failures, and any path that persists individual updates.

threats.label: Inference from releases
threats.detail: An observer uses repeated aggregate models to infer whether a person or record influenced training.
threats.observableSignal: Track cumulative privacy spend, release frequency, clipping rates, canary leakage tests, and membership-inference results.

threats.label: Poisoning client
threats.detail: A participant sends a crafted update to degrade the global model or implant a backdoor.
threats.observableSignal: Monitor clipped-update rates, aggregate direction shifts, slice regressions, backdoor probes, and contributor reputation.

threats.label: Dropout manipulation
threats.detail: Clients disappear strategically so a round aborts or the surviving cohort becomes biased.
threats.observableSignal: Measure survivor margin, aborts by cohort and region, repeated participant patterns, and selection-distribution drift.

defenseStacks.label: Local data only
defenseStacks.detail: Authenticated transport, but the coordinator receives individual updates.
protections: Raw examples remain on participating clients
Authenticated encrypted transport protects messages on the network
defenseStacks.limitation: Individual updates and repeated aggregate releases can still leak information; data locality does not constrain poisoning or strategic dropout.

defenseStacks.label: Secure aggregation
defenseStacks.detail: The coordinator learns a threshold aggregate rather than each surviving update.
protections: Authenticated transport and threshold secure aggregation
Individual surviving updates are hidden from the coordinator
A minimum survivor set is required before unmasking the aggregate
defenseStacks.limitation: The released aggregate has no formal statistical privacy bound, and hidden individual updates make poisoning diagnosis harder without compatible safeguards.

defenseStacks.label: Secure aggregate + DP
defenseStacks.detail: Clip contributions, aggregate securely, and add accounted noise to the released update.
protections: Threshold secure aggregation hides individual updates
Differential privacy constrains leakage from released aggregates
A versioned accountant tracks cumulative releases
defenseStacks.limitation: Privacy noise does not stop targeted poisoning, Sybil participation, biased client selection, or round-abort attacks.

defenseStacks.label: Hardened release stack
defenseStacks.detail: Add eligibility, contribution bounds, integrity checks, cohort monitoring, canaries, and rollback.
protections: Secure aggregation and accounted differential privacy
Attested clients, rate limits, and identity-aware eligibility
Norm bounds, aggregate anomaly checks, and poisoning canaries
Cohort-quality gates, survivor monitoring, and rollback
defenseStacks.limitation: No generic stack proves safety against adaptive attackers; robust aggregation, secure aggregation, and privacy mechanisms must be designed and evaluated together.
